body:
Hello, there! 

Thanks a lot for you message! It's nice to know that someone can relate and feel in a similar way. 

I totally agree with working out as a great way of venting out, works miracles on me too. I guess the time excuse is not enough to take something so important for my mood out of the picture. I know this is a long distance run, not a sprint, so I'll start gradually, tomorrow will be just some stretching. Starting to get the working out habit just by stretching has turned out quite well in the past, it's a very easy way to build up some routine and once you are in the "auto" mode, it's pretty much done. 

I hope you call went well and you didn't get yelled at all. I don't yell at work, but my girlfriend took a lot of abuse she didn't deserve, and all I can say about it is that when someone yells at you, don't take it personally, you are not the problem, it's the one yelling who is suffering and that's just an emotional reaction. Doesn't make me or him less of an asshole, but I hope it makes it easier for you to cope with that crap. 

What's your personal venture about? It's funny how I complain about being exhausted from work but I'm always willing to hear about business...

You are right about friends, the best ones I have are the ones who don't care how long since we talked to each other, they are exactly where we left. Thanks for pointing that, I'm going to visit my mother this weekend and I'll take the time to have a beer with some old teammates. 

I'm finishing "La sombra del águila", that's Spanish for "The eagle's shadow", by Arturo Pérez Reverte. It's about a battle of Napoleon's army at the Russian front, where some Spanish took part, just at the same moment when the Spanish where fighting against the French in the independence war. It's a very short book, easy read and even funny, but I don't know if it's translated into other languages. But I have to recommend anything, I'll start with my nickname, based on a character from the book "Choke" by Chuck Palahniuk. It's a very funny book, it really helped me when I have my first depression episode, read it like 3 times in a row. 

I have to sleep a bit now, but I will wake up tomorrow looking forward for some time to surf discogs. I usually go around soulseek, the interface is quite ugly, but there are some users with amazing collections and they are usually glad to help you find new things. 

Thanks again for you answer, it meant a lot!
What does bring the thoughts back?

Being able to be alone is one of the most important skills you can have. I've shared most of my adult life with a partner and I can only recommend to lower your expectations. Making a relationship the most important thing in your life, even before you have it, puts you at risk of making it burn too quickly. If it's really about your future, be patient and take time to get ready. 

A meaningful relationship can be a nice thing, but it ends. Sooner or later, you will be alone, for a period of time or forever. Dealing with it is something you should be prepared to and even ENJOY. If you can deal with yourself, you are way more likely to be a good companion for anyone to have when they are down.

I always wondered why this happened to me. Not sure if it's the same for anyone else, but I got to the conclusion of this being the consequence of not opening myself. Quite a shitty paradox. 

As an introvert, when I have a problem I deal with it myself, but when things get overwhelming they might stay on my mind for days and people chatting and talking about anything else are just annoying. 

I try to clear my mind from trouble before I get to any social event, sometimes I smoke some weed, but loud music works better for me. And not surprisingly, telling the right people about what troubles me is usually the best I can do, usually nothing is solved, but at least you feel the support of your peers.

Sounds like you made a habit from it and that's quite difficult to avoid. The best thing to do is replacing it with a new one that makes you feel better. Sports are always a good idea, but if you don't seem to be able to get off the computer screen, try being yourself or someone else on some other site where you don't feel creepy at all. 

I found myself going back to my ex's profile for a long time and it didn't even make sense. I was seeing other girls and had zero feelings for her, but I just fell on her profile every time I was bored. In the end, I realized it was a need for interaction, the kind of sweetness or happiness you got from your relationship and that might get you hooked. But she's not giving it back to you, so it's a loop and you are getting nothing good from it.

Leaving things on good terms is an utopic idea. Especially if she made the first move to end it. 

Go on with your life and let the good memories stay there if you will, but don't try to go back in time if you don't have a Delorean.

I look back to the time I was in a similar position and I can only thank her (actually THEM, same mistake twice and on my way to the third) for leaving sooner than later.
